subject: Observability & Evals: diagnostic recap, success criteria, and rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Infra <infra@fintechco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Observability & Evals: diagnostic recap, success criteria, and rollout guardrails

Hi Maria / Fintech infra team —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call, plus proposed next steps so we can align on a scoping plan:

High-level pain points you shared
- Hard to detect model regressions tied to prompt/conditioning changes; manual spot-checking today.
- Unpredictable tail latency during high-concurrency hours (impacts UX on loan approvals).
- No unified visibility across hosted vendor calls + in-house models (split dashboards).

Current stack notes you mentioned
- Primary serving: in-house inference (CPU-based microservices) behind a proxy; some GPU jobs for batch scoring.
- Monitoring: Prometheus + Datadog for infra, but no token-level cost traces.
- Experimentation: ad-hoc golden prompt sets stored in a Git repo.

Success criteria you called out
- Regression detection: identify quality regressions within 24 hours on core prompts (priority set).
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for interactive flows during peak windows.
- Cost visibility: token-level spend buckets per route and model variant.

Specific observability & evals asks (from today)
1) Dashboards: a set of 4 starter dashboards (overall health, latency by route/model, golden-prompt performance cohorting, token-cost decomposition).
2) Tracing hooks: distributed traces that tie request -> model variant -> token counts (we recommended OpenTelemetry + light-weight tracing shim).
3) Golden prompts: capture a canonical set (we discussed ~120 prompts across high/med/low buckets) and automate daily evals.
4) Regression alerts: threshold-based alerts + automated regression emails to owners; run baseline nightly and surface candidate regressions.
5) Rollout guardrails: canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on perf/regression triggers.

Attachments: I dropped a first-cut diagnostic matrix and a seed golden-prompts file (see attached: fintechco-observability-matrix.xlsx, golden-prompts-v1.json).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Action: Redwood tech assessment and timeline (deliverable: tech-assessment doc + proposed dashboard wireframes) — due in 4 business days. Owner: Grace (PM+sales).
- Action: Instrumentation checklist for tracing hooks — due in 6 business days. Owner: Dev Patel (engineering).
- Action: Confirm golden prompt canonicalization rules (who owns, cadence) — due in 3 business days. Owner: Maria / FintechCo.

Would you confirm those owners and the priority for the 120 prompts (we can start with the 30 highest-volume prompts)? If that looks good I'll schedule a short follow-up working session next week to align on owners and timing.

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

—
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Grace —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications and a small ask:

Clarifications
- The 120 prompt set is correct; please prioritize the "loan-approval" and "KYC-summary" cohorts first (roughly 30 prompts total).
- Our current pre-prod stack will permit tracing shims but we cannot add heavy SDK agents to production without security sign-off. So lightweight OTEL traces are preferred.

Success criteria — add one item
- Business impact: demonstrable reduction in manual QA volume by 40% within the first quarter of running nightly evals.

Ask
- Can Redwood include an estimated cost delta for enabling tracing hooks (infra + token tracking) vs. a minimal sampling approach? We'll need that for procurement.

I've attached our internal draft SLA excerpt that calls out latency targets we use for other real-time services (fintechco-sla-draft.pdf).

I'll confirm owner for prompt canonicalization by EOD tomorrow; for now assign to me tentatively.

Appreciate the fast follow-up.

Best,
Maria

Subject: Fwd: Observability & Evals: diagnostic recap, success criteria, and rollout guardrails

Folks — forwarding the FintechCo discovery thread. Key asks below and initial prioritization proposal.

Key asks (actionable)
- Tracing hooks (OTEL shim) that emit: request id, model variant, route, token count, and top-level latency buckets.
- Grafana dashboards: health, latency by route/model, golden-prompt diffs, token-cost breakdown.
- Eval pipeline: nightly batch run over canonical prompts, surface regressions + candidate diffs.
- Rollout policy: canary -> incremental -> full with automatic rollback triggers.

Priority proposal
1) Instrumentation checklist + low-overhead PoC (Dev) — 3 business days
2) Tech assessment + dashboard wireframes (Grace + Dev) — 4 business days
3) Golden prompt mapping & initial cohort (Karthik + Maria) — 3 business days

Questions for you both before I lock calendar slots:
- Dev: can you confirm whether we should use sampling (1%) for production traces initially or try to emit token counts for all requests?
- Karthik: will you lead on defining the cohort segmentation for golden prompts (high/medium/low volume)?

I'll book a 30-min working session for Thursday morning; please propose a slot if that does not work.

—
Grace

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:17:06 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability & Evals: diagnostic recap, success criteria, and rollout guardrails

Thanks Grace — I'll take ownership of the tracing hooks and the PoC instrumentation checklist. Quick replies to questions: 

- Sampling vs full emit: for production start, do sampling (1%) + targeted full emit for the loan-approval route (we can escalate to full emit after sign-off). Sampling keeps cost and perf low during initial rollout.
- Token counts: we can emit token counts as part of the trace envelope (lightweight counter) without adding heavy payloads; Dev team can deliver a shim for the proxy to emit these.
- Dashboards: I'll scope Grafana panels for p50/p95/p99, request volume, token-cost per route, and golden-prompt diff chart.

Deliverables and owners (confirming)
- Instrumentation checklist + PoC shim (Dev Patel) — PR with tests in 3 business days.
- Dashboard wireframes (Grace + Dev) — internal mockups in 4 business days.
- Eval pipeline start script + nightly runner (Dev + Karthik) — initial runner in 6 business days.

I'll start a draft repo (infra/fintechco-observability) and share access link once created.

Dev
